title: Simultaneous random polytope approximation characterizes the Euclidean ball
summary: In this work, we present a new geometric characterization of the Euclidean ball based on approximation by random polytopes. We investigate when a single boundary sampling density is asymptotically optimal for two random polytope approximation problems, and show that for a convex body in $\R^d$ with $C^2$ boundary and everywhere positive principal curvatures, one fixed density minimizes the leading expected errors for any two distinct intrinsic volume differences of inscribed random polytopes if and only if the body is a Euclidean ball.
